description: Generates white noise - a pure generator with NO audio input (input_arity 0; call process() without an input argument). Output duration is set exactly by dur (sample-exact: 2.0 -> 88200 frames at 44.1 kHz). NOT stochastic in the reproducibility sense: there is no seed flag and no clock seeding - identical parameters produce byte-identical output on every run (verified back-to-back and 1.2 s apart), so the 'random' material is a fixed sequence; amp scales that same sequence exactly linearly (amp 0.25 output = 0.25 x the amp-1 output). Multi-channel output via chans (banner claims 1, 2 or 4; the binary enforces 1-16 and all render, verified to 16 channels). RMS at amp 1 is about -4.8 dBFS - hot; stage headroom before mixing.
musical_use: The subtractive-synthesis and test-signal source: render a noise bed, then carve it - filter bank arpeggiation, formants put vowel motion, envel impose rhythm, hilite trace reduction. Because output is deterministic, a noise bed is reproducible across a whole session (and cache-friendly); for DIFFERENT noise takes there is no seed to vary - render at a longer dur and cut, or process divergently downstream. Time-varying amp (breakpoint) turns the generator into shaped noise directly - swells, stabs, and fades without a second enveloping pass. Keep amp around 0.3-0.7 when the bed will be summed with other material (submix mix wraps on overload). chans > 1 renders dual-mono (every channel bit-identical) - for real stereo width, filter or process two renders differently and pair them with submix interleave.

srate.description: Output sample rate. The binary quotes an enforced range '(16000.000000 to 192000.000000)' but actually accepts a discrete set: 16000, 22050, 24000, 32000, 44100, 48000, 88200, 96000 (44000 refused 'ERROR: INVALID DATA / ERROR: Invalid sample rate.'; 176400/192000 refused despite the quoted range; the banner lists yet another set). Entry default 44100 - always emitted (positional).

chans.description: Output channel count. DIVERGENCE: the banner says 'can be 1, 2 or 4' but the binary enforces '(1.000000 to 16.000000)' and every value 1-16 renders (3, 5, 8, 16 all verified, correct channel counts). Multi-channel output is DUAL-MONO: every channel is bit-identical (verified at 2 and 4 channels) - chans > 1 buys no width.

dur.description: Output duration in seconds - sets the output length exactly (sample-exact). CDP-enforced range '(0.040000 to 7200.000000)'; the engine's own duration cap (default 300 s) applies first via the set_by pre-flight. Required.

amp.description: Output amplitude, CDP-enforced '(0.000000 to 1.000000)' (omitted = 1.0). CDP accepts -a0 but renders digital silence (output verification would fail) - curated min keeps it nonzero. BREAKPOINT-CAPABLE (banner: 'Amp may vary through time'; verified: a 0->1 ramp renders with first-100ms RMS at 6% of last-100ms). With no audio input, relative-time breakpoint envelopes compile against the OUTPUT duration (the dur parameter).

examples.description: A 3-second mono noise bed for subtractive carving.
examples.expected_use: No input argument. Deterministic: rendering it twice gives byte-identical files.

examples.description: Shaped noise swell via time-varying amplitude.
examples.expected_use: The envelope's relative times map onto dur (0-4 s): rise to full by 2.8 s, fall to near-silence at the end.

known_issues: Deterministic 'randomness': no seed flag exists and runs are byte-identical regardless of spacing (verified 1.2 s apart) - the opposite trap to clock-seeded programs. Two calls with identical params give THE SAME noise; there is no way to get a fresh take from the binary itself.

amp 0 is accepted by CDP but renders digital silence, which fails the engine's output verification - hence the curated nonzero minimum. amp scaling is exactly linear (amp 0.25 = 0.25 x the amp-1 render, verified to 1 LSB).

The sample-rate parameter's quoted range (16000-192000) is not the truth: only the discrete set 16000/22050/24000/32000/44100/48000/88200/96000 is accepted, and the banner lists a third variant of the set. Divergences recorded from the binary.
chans 1-16 all work despite the banner's '1, 2 or 4'.
A '-f' (float output) flag appears in third-party documentation (afta8) but not in this binary's banner; passing it is accepted and IGNORED (output stays PCM_16) - not exposed.

Generator entry: process() takes no input argument here; graph()/batch()/sweep() refuse arity-0 entries with a structured error (arity_zero_unsupported) - run the generator first, then wire its output.
